content: 1. Hamilton RG discussed the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and diagnostic approaches for latex allergy in a comprehensive review published on the UpToDate website between 2014 and 2016. 2. Casanova LM and colleagues conducted a study assessing the risk of self-contamination during the removal of personal protective equipment (PPE) used in the care of Ebola patients. Their findings, published in Infection Control & Hospital Epidemiology in 2016, highlighted critical areas for improving safety protocols. 3. This cross-sectional study, published in PLOS Medicine in 2017, provided valuable insights into responder health and immunity. 4. Reidy P and colleagues developed a PPE solution tailored for UK military medical personnel working in Ebola treatment units in Sierra Leone. Their findings, published in Journal of Hospital Infection in 2017, emphasized the importance of specialized protective equipment in high-risk environments. 5. Cummings KJ and team addressed infection prevention and control strategies in the first U.S. community hospital to care for Ebola patients. Their work, published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2016, provided a framework for national recommendations and future strategies. 6. Their study, published in Antimicrobial Resistance and Infection Control in 2016, discussed the implications of such practices on public health. 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) released comprehensive guidelines on hand hygiene in healthcare settings in 2009, emphasizing its critical role in infection prevention. 8. Casanova LM and collaborators assessed viral transfer risks during the doffing of Ebola-level PPE in a biocontainment unit. Their study, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2018, identified key areas for protocol improvement. 9. Olu O and colleagues conducted a retrospective descriptive study on the epidemiology of Ebola virus transmission among healthcare workers in Sierra Leone from May to December 2014. 10. 11. This case series, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2015, provided early evidence of potential therapeutic options. 12. The WHO and International Labour Organization (ILO) jointly developed a guide in 2022 for implementing occupational health and safety programs for healthcare workers, emphasizing the importance of protecting those on the frontlines. 13. Samai M and colleagues evaluated the safety and tolerability of the rVSV-ZEBOV-GP vaccine during the West African Ebola outbreak. Their findings, published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases, contributed to the understanding of vaccine deployment in outbreak settings. 14. Their work was published in The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene and The Journal of Infectious Diseases. 15. Their study, published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2020, highlighted occupational vulnerabilities. 16. Gsell P-S and colleagues reported on the operational and safety outcomes of ring vaccination with rVSV-ZEBOV during the 2016 Ebola outbreak in Guinea. Published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017, the study demonstrated the effectiveness of targeted vaccination strategies. 17. Dunn AC and team investigated nosocomial transmission of Ebola virus disease in pediatric and maternity wards in Sierra Leone in 2014. Their findings, published in American Journal of Infection Control in 2016, emphasized the need for robust infection control practices. 18. Matanoch A and collaborators analyzed Ebola virus disease cases among healthcare workers not working in treatment units in Liberia. Their study, published in 2014, highlighted gaps in infection prevention outside specialized facilities. 19. Cook BWM and colleagues examined the disinfection characteristics of Ebola virus variants during outbreaks. Their findings, published in Scientific Reports in 2016, provided critical data on effective decontamination methods. 20. Schuit M and team compared the stability of different Ebola virus strains in blood. Their study, published in PLOS One in 2016, contributed to understanding the virus's environmental persistence. 21. Bibby K and collaborators evaluated the disinfection of Ebola virus in municipal wastewater. Their study, published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2017, addressed public health concerns related to waste management. 22. Youkee D and colleagues assessed environmental contamination and decontamination practices in an Ebola holding unit in Sierra Leone. Their findings, published in PLOS One in 2015, informed infection control protocols. 23. Bausch DG and team evaluated the risk of Ebola virus transmission from bodily fluids and fomites. Their study, published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2007, provided foundational data on transmission dynamics. 24. Puro V and collaborators investigated the persistence of Ebola virus on surfaces after cleaning procedures in high-level isolation settings. Their findings, published in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology in 2016, emphasized the importance of thorough decontamination. 25. Palich R and colleagues detected Ebola virus RNA on fomites near confirmed patients in Guinea. Their study, published in PLOS One in 2017, highlighted the potential for environmental transmission. 26. Wu X and team investigated environmental contamination in an Ebola convalescent ward. Their findings, published in The Journal of Hospital Infection in 2015, underscored the need for rigorous cleaning protocols. 27. Gallandat K and collaborators systematically reviewed the efficacy of chlorine-based surface disinfection methods. Their study, published in American Journal of Infection Control in 2021, provided evidence-based recommendations for outbreak settings. 28. The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) published a list of disinfectants effective against emerging viral pathogens, including Ebola, to guide public health responses. 29. Lantagne D and colleagues evaluated the efficacy, safety, and suitability of disinfectants for preventing infectious disease transmission. Their findings, published in Water in 2018, informed public health practices. 30. Edmunds KL and team developed recommendations for managing waste contaminated with Ebola virus using a hazard analysis approach. Their study, published in Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2016, addressed critical waste management challenges. 31. Garibaldi BT and collaborators described the creation of a biocontainment unit at a tertiary care hospital, detailing their experience in managing high-risk infectious diseases. Their work, published in Annals of the American Thoracic Society in 2016, provided a model for other institutions. 32. Sterk E and colleagues published the 2008 Filovirus Hemorrhagic Fever Guidelines, offering comprehensive recommendations for managing outbreaks. 33. The WHO released key questions and answers concerning healthcare waste management during the Ebola outbreak, emphasizing safe practices to minimize risks. 34. Dietz PM and team analyzed the epidemiology and risk factors for Ebola virus disease in Sierra Leone from May 2014 to January 2015. Their findings, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases, provided critical insights into outbreak dynamics. 35. Their findings, published in PLOS Medicine, informed targeted intervention strategies. 36. Senga M and collaborators identified factors underlying Ebola virus infection among health workers in Sierra Leone. 37. Muoghalu IS and team analyzed the transmission chain of the 2014–2015 Ebola outbreak in Sierra Leone. Their observational study, published in Frontiers in Public Health, provided insights into outbreak control. 38. Tiffany A and colleagues quantified the impact of safe and dignified burials during the West African Ebola epidemic. Their study, published in American Journal of Infectious Diseases, emphasized the importance of culturally sensitive practices. 39. Lee-Kwan SH and team identified facilitators and barriers to community acceptance of safe medical burials during the Ebola epidemic in Sierra Leone. Their findings, published in Journal of Health Communication, informed public health strategies. 40. Their mixed-methods study, published in BMC Public Health, provided actionable insights for outbreak management. 41. Lyons P and team engaged religious leaders to promote safe burial practices during the Ebola outbreak in Sierra Leone. Their study, published in Bulletin of the World Health Organization, highlighted the role of community leaders in public health interventions. 42. Sikakuly FK and colleagues explored the socio-cultural and anthropological implications of safe and dignified burials for Ebola victims in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Their study, published in One Health, emphasized the importance of cultural considerations in outbreak response. 43. Gautier L and collaborators evaluated a community-led prevention strategy to enhance behavioral changes toward Ebola prevention in Côte d'Ivoire. Their qualitative case study, published in Global Health Research and Policy, demonstrated the effectiveness of community engagement. 44. Ratnayake R and team reviewed targeted spatiotemporal interventions against cholera epidemics, providing insights applicable to Ebola outbreak management. Their findings, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, emphasized the importance of localized responses. 45. Dahl BA and colleagues documented the CDC’s response to the 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Their report, published in MMWR, highlighted key challenges and successes. 46. Their study, published in BMC Medicine, identified critical areas for improvement. 47. Mobula LM and collaborators provided recommendations for the COVID-19 response based on lessons learned from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Their findings, published in American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene, emphasized the importance of preparedness. 48. Hall S and colleagues evaluated the use of ultraviolet fluorescence-based simulation to assess PPE effectiveness for healthcare workers managing high-consequence infectious diseases. Their study, published in Journal of Hospital Infection, informed PPE training protocols. 49. Honda H and Iwata K reviewed strategies to improve PPE compliance among healthcare workers in high-risk settings. Their findings, published in Current Opinion in Infectious Diseases, emphasized the importance of training and monitoring. 50. Kilinc FS reviewed the properties of isolation gowns used in healthcare, providing insights into fabric and gown performance. Their study, published in Journal of Engineered Fibers and Fabrics, informed PPE selection. 51. Lee YA and colleagues assessed PPE needs for healthcare workers, emphasizing the importance of adequate supplies and training. Their findings, published in Health Science Reports, highlighted gaps in preparedness. 52. Kilinc-Balci FS and collaborators evaluated the performance of isolation gowns, providing recommendations for their use in healthcare settings. Their study, published in American Journal of Infection Control, informed PPE standards. 53. McLaws M-L and team proposed a highly precautionary doffing sequence for healthcare workers managing Ebola patients. Their study, published in American Journal of Infection Control, aimed to reduce occupational risks. 54. Andonian J and colleagues evaluated the impact of teamwork training on preventing self-contamination during PPE doffing. Their findings, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases, emphasized the importance of collaborative training. 55. Bell T and team used fluorescent markers to assess contamination risks during PPE use. Their study, published in ID Cases, provided practical insights for improving safety protocols. 56. Kwon JH and collaborators assessed healthcare worker protocol deviations and self-contamination during PPE donning and doffing. Their findings, published in Infection Control & Hospital Epidemiology, highlighted areas for improvement. 57. Lim SM and team investigated contamination risks during PPE doffing by healthcare providers. Their study, published in Clinical and Experimental Emergency Medicine, emphasized the need for rigorous training. 58. Mumma JM and colleagues conducted a human factors risk analysis of a doffing protocol for Ebola-level PPE. Their findings, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases, identified common errors and contamination risks. 59. Wolfe MK and collaborators conducted a randomized trial investigating the impact of handwashing methods on skin irritation and dermatitis in communities facing Ebola. Their study, published in PLOS One, informed hand hygiene recommendations. 60. Gao P and team evaluated the effect of alcohol-based hand rubs on the tensile properties of medical gloves. Their findings, published in Journal of Occupational and Environmental Hygiene, informed glove selection and usage. 61. Tomori O and colleagues conducted a serologic survey among healthcare workers during the 1995 Ebola outbreak in Kikwit, Democratic Republic of Congo. Their study, published in Journal of Infectious Diseases, provided insights into occupational risks. 62. Lopez MA and team analyzed the first secondary case of Ebola outside Africa, focusing on epidemiological characteristics and contact monitoring in Spain. Their findings, published in Euro Surveillance, informed international outbreak responses. 63. Musa EO and collaborators documented the epidemiological profile of the Ebola outbreak in Nigeria in 2014. Their study, published in The Pan African Medical Journal, highlighted the importance of rapid response. 64. Ngatu NR and colleagues reviewed the epidemiology of Ebola virus disease and occupational risks for healthcare workers in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings, published in Journal of Epidemiology, emphasized the need for strengthened public health preparedness. 65. Amadin J compared the effectiveness of disinfectant-impregnated wipes versus detergent wipes for surface decontamination. Their study, published in 2021, provided practical recommendations for infection control. 66. String GM and collaborators evaluated the efficacy of chlorine against bacteriophage Phi6, a surrogate for enveloped human viruses, on various surfaces. Their findings, published in Journal of Environmental Science and Health, informed disinfection practices. 67. Julian TR and team assessed the efficacy of field-generated electrochemical oxidants for disinfecting fomites. Their study, published in Food and Environmental Virology, provided insights into practical disinfection methods. 68. Rutala WA and colleagues evaluated cleaning and disinfection methods against Clostridium difficile spores, emphasizing the importance of physical removal. Their findings, published in Infection Control & Hospital Epidemiology, informed cleaning protocols. 69. Swanson KC and team analyzed contact tracing performance during the Ebola epidemic in Liberia. Their findings, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases, highlighted the importance of effective contact tracing. 70. The IPC ring approach, developed for managing Ebola and Marburg disease cases, emphasizes early cluster detection and localized responses to reduce transmission. While promising, its effectiveness depends on robust IPC training, contact tracing, and triage capacities.
